title: Evaluating Corporate Leverage Ratios, Covenant Triggers & Counterparty Stress Testing
summary: A practical banking risk framework for evaluating corporate leverage, liquidity buffers, and counterparty exposure under macroeconomic volatility.
architecture_flow: Financial Statements -> Ratio Analysis (D/E, Current, ICR) -> Stress Testing -> Credit Risk Tier

sections.heading: The Core Pillars of Credit Underwriting
sections.body: Assessing leverage, liquidity, and profitability provides a baseline, but rigorous credit underwriting requires dynamic scenario modeling under adverse shocks.

sections.heading: Monitoring Covenants & Early Warning Indicators
sections.body: Tracking interest coverage and cash flow conversion cycles flags potential distress well before formal covenant breaches occur.

sections.heading: Audit-Ready Documentation & Regulatory QC
sections.body: Maintaining pristine documentation trails ensures full compliance with institutional risk frameworks and supervisory standards.

takeaway: Combining quantitative ratio thresholds with qualitative governance safeguards institutional loan portfolios against unexpected defaults.

title: Panel Data Regression & Policy Evaluation: Overcoming Omitted Variable Bias
summary: How fixed-effects panel estimation and stationarity testing in R and Stata isolate true economic policy impacts from macro time trends.
architecture_flow: Panel Dataset -> ADF Stationarity Test -> First Differencing -> Fixed Effects (Entity/Time) -> Elasticity Estimate

sections.heading: Stationarity and Unit Root Diagnostics
sections.body: Running Augmented Dickey-Fuller tests prevents spurious regressions when analyzing multi-year macroeconomic time series.

sections.heading: Entity and Time Fixed Effects
sections.body: Including unit-specific and temporal dummy controls removes unobserved heterogeneity and unmeasured confounding variables.

takeaway: Proper econometric specification is essential to distinguish causal policy effectiveness from coincidental macro trends.
